finding.claim: /checkout computes the charge total from client-supplied item price and qty, so the attacker sets the price. They can pay 0.01, or send a negative price or qty to make the total zero or negative, which may refund or credit the account depending on how charge handles negative amounts.
finding.source: req.body.items[].price and req.body.items[].qty (authenticated user's JSON body)

trace.note: total = sum(i.price * i.qty) using values taken directly from the request body
total is passed to the payment charge with no server-side price lookup or validation
the attacker-influenced total is returned as the charged amount

finding.guards_checked: No catalog price lookup, no check that price/qty are positive or numeric, and no auth middleware in this file. The sibling route /checkout-v2 shows the intended pattern (price from req.catalog.price, qty clamped to at least 1), which this route lacks.

verdict.guard_found: none (no validation, no catalog lookup on /checkout; only /checkout-v2 at cart.js:13-14 has them; auth middleware is not in this repo, req.user is assumed to be set upstream)
verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty and cart.js:6 passes it to req.payments.charge with no validation or catalog lookup, unlike /checkout-v2 at cart.js:13-14, so any authenticated user controls the charged amount.
